correctness.rationale: Both the frozen formula and the retained result are correct. After conditioning on, and rotating by, the angle of a labelled sample, independent uniform residual points become ordered uniform arguments and their differences have constant simplex density (n-1)!. The chord is 2 sin(pi x), even for a gap over a semicircle. The diagonal comes from the Beta(1,n-1) marginal and sin^2=(1-cos(2·))/2. At fixed two-gap sum z, integrating sin(pi x) sin(pi(z-x)) over x from 0 to z gives [sin(pi z)/pi-z cos(pi z)]/2; the two-gap density supplies (n-1)(n-2)(1-z)^(n-3). Replacing z(1-z)^(n-3) by the difference of successive powers gives exactly (s_n-r_n)/2. Counting ordered terms gives the asserted variance. The J expression follows from the integral exponential Taylor remainder with factor (ia)^(k+1)/k!. An independent symbolic replay, python3 /workspace/review_work/reproduce_4.py, verified the two small exact cases by direct simplex integration and the expansions of the power-sum covariances. The original higher-order variance is also correct: the cubic variance has coefficients (360,-6048,60552) at orders 5–7, the cubic–quintic covariance leads at 28800 n^-7, the quintic variance is O(n^-9), and the seventh-power remainder is O in L2 of n^-6, giving covariance with the centered cubic term O(n^-17/2). The revised files retain these coefficients only as a credited consequence, not as a separate finding. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: The surviving finite formula gives the exact sampling uncertainty of the standard chord-sum estimator of circle length, at sample sizes where a leading asymptotic is only approximate. It captures dependence between different chords and replaces a simplex double integral or a power-series resummation by a number of elementary finite sums independent of the number of gap pairs. The value is the arbitrary-n variance evaluation, not the covered asymptotic correction or rederiving one already known small case. No numerical conditioning guarantee is asserted.
